source.title: Sparse Feature Policy Unlearning Mitigates State Hallucination in Vision-Language-Action Models
source.authors: Ji-Ho Lee; Jeongeun Park; Heayoun Choi; Taekyung Kim; Eunwoo Kim

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE analysis to visual-token activations in VLA policies, a new model setting, and reports feature associations with execution outcomes.
record.gate_note: The study measures SAE feature activations in VLA policies and reports their association with hallucination and successful execution, as well as activation changes after unlearning. Task-success and hallucination-rate results are not rows because they do not measure a claim version. SAE dimensions and active-feature counts are setup details, not results about superposition geometry.
record.test_reason: The study uses Top-k SAEs as a tool. It picks features that correlate with execution outcomes in VLA visual-token activations, then uses them as unlearning targets, and reports mostly the unlearning method's performance. It reports no evidence on whether the activations contain recoverable sparse features (no reconstruction, interpretability or dictionary-quality results) and nothing on how features spread across neurons. The feature–outcome associations concern a different question: whether a feature predicts behaviour, not whether the representation is superposed or sparse.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that state hallucination coincides with weaker attention to task-relevant regions and distinct region-conditioned sparse-feature patterns. They report that SOUL, which suppresses hallucination features and reinforces success features, cuts hallucination (average 55.0% to 33.5%) and raises clean success while preserving 89% of prior successes.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Top-k SAEs to analyze visual-token activations and guides LoRA policy unlearning in VLA models; it does not reproduce the toy-network superposition experiments or measure their overlap geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature selection spatial granularity changes results: region-guided selection outperforms global and tokenized selection in the reported average benchmark comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected SAE features in VLA visual-token activations differ in activation between hallucination-failure and clean-success rollouts (Fig. 3; boxplots, no numbers).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features of VLA policies carry behaviour-predictive signals usable as targets for unlearning or steering.

record.problems: Feature-activation results are primarily qualitative and presented in figures without numerical activation values or stated uncertainty. The study does not test SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonicality.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant feature-activation results were left out. Benchmark hallucination and task-success metrics were not included as rows because they do not measure any listed claim version.

untested.parts: All parts: toy models, geometry, sparsity transition.
All parts: capacity competition, dedicated dimensions.
Distribution of features across neurons. SAE recoverability and quality: no reconstruction or interpretability metrics are reported.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. Using an SAE and finding outcome-correlated features does not test whether models contain sparse, dictionary-recoverable features. Rows r3–r10 report changes that the training objective directly optimizes.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more sparse features than dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric arrangements.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons can arise without capacity pressure or whether they are evidence of superposition.
The study analyzes VLA visual-token activations, not LLMs generally; it does not measure feature spreading across neurons.
SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status as units of the model.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.operation_detail: Compared region-conditioned SAE feature activation across clean-success, hallucination-failure, and non-hallucination-failure rollouts.
rows.measure: Rollout-level maximum region-conditioned activation of the selected SAE feature
rows.note: The text reports that the feature remains weak in clean-success rollouts and becomes strongly activated around hallucination events in hallucination-failure rollouts.
rows.check: This is a selected feature's correlation with hallucination outcomes, a selection-style result. It does not measure whether sparse features are recoverable from the model. The subject is not stated (models are OpenVLA/π0.5), and there are no numbers (figure only).

rows.subject: OpenVLA
rows.operation_detail: Applied SOUL policy unlearning using selected SAE features, then compared feature activations before and after unlearning.

rows.note: The text reports suppression of forget-feature activation after unlearning.
rows.check: This is the study's own method's effect on activations. SOUL directly optimizes to suppress forget features, so the change holds by construction and bears on no version.
